prerequisites: Basic course in analysis of dynamic systems (continuous and discrete)
Basic knowledge of differential and integral calculus

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the fundamentals of signal digitalization.
Know the Discrete Fourier Transform and its properties.
Be able to perform spectral analysis.
Be able to design digital filters for specific applications.

syllabus_topics: Origins and applications of DSP. Basic concepts of signals and noise.
Analog-digital conversion: Shannon's Theorem. Analog filters. Antialiasing filtering.
Digital filtering. Design and application of filters.
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as (0.40 × E) + (0.6 × T), where E is the written exam and T represents course assignments. There is no minimum grade required for course assignments. The extraordinary call consists of a single written exam covering all course content, and the grade obtained in this exam will be the final grade. In case of doubt regarding the authorship of any assessable test or the use of unauthorized means, students may be asked for an in-person defense.
